title: Adaptive Fluid Cohomology on Surfaces
summary: Simulating inviscid, incompressible fluids on non-simply-connected curved surfaces requires careful treatment of the flow's local and global behavior. While recent theoretical advancements have established the critical dynamics of the harmonic component in such flows, practical applications remain computationally restricted by a lack of spatial and temporal adaptivity. Furthermore, simulations on poor-quality meshes often lead to numerical instability and a failure to preserve the flow's underlying harmonic component when using naive interpolation methods. In this paper, we introduce Adaptive Fluid Cohomology, a framework that integrates dynamic spatial and temporal refinement into the simulation of the Euler equations. We leverage a posteriori error estimation to adjust spatial resolution on the fly, alongside a standard Dormand-Prince 5(4) time-stepping scheme for temporal accuracy. To ensure stability during mesh mutations, we develop a novel method that robustly transfers the harmonic basis during remeshing. While our experimental evaluation focuses on 2D surface flows, the underlying theoretical formulation is presented to capture the 3D setting as well. Our evaluation demonstrates that this adaptive approach accurately recreates the dynamics of high-resolution simulations while reducing the memory footprint by up to 86% and maintaining numerical stability even on poor-quality triangulations where static methods fail.

AI.tldr: Adaptive Fluid Cohomology introduces dynamic spatial and temporal refinement for inviscid, incompressible fluid simulations on non-simply-connected curved surfaces, using a posteriori error estimation and a novel harmonic basis transfer method to achieve 86% memory reduction while maintaining stability on poor-quality meshes.
AI.motivation: Existing fluid simulations lack spatial and temporal adaptivity, and naive interpolation on poor-quality meshes fails to preserve harmonic components, leading to numerical instability.
AI.method: The framework integrates a posteriori error estimation for spatial resolution adjustment, Dormand-Prince 5(4) time-stepping, and a novel harmonic basis transfer method for robust remeshing during mesh mutations.
AI.result: Experimental evaluation on 2D surface flows demonstrates accurate recreation of high-resolution dynamics, 86% memory reduction, and numerical stability on poor-quality triangulations where static methods fail.
AI.conclusion: The adaptive approach effectively captures both local and global flow behavior while maintaining computational efficiency, with theoretical formulation applicable to 3D surface flows.

title: MetaInfer: A Knowledge Only LLM Inference Engine Generator SKILL Toolbox
summary: As LLM technology advances, the space of model families, compute hardware, quantization schemes, parallelization strategies, and specialized optimization kernels continues to expand, sharply increasing the code complexity and maintenance cost of general-purpose inference frameworks. Conventional software engineering uses multiple layers of abstraction to support diverse application scenarios, but these abstractions also increase system complexity and may introduce additional performance overhead. This paper presents metainfer, an 'LLM-as-Compiler' approach in which users specify only the runtime constraints of an inference program. An LLM-driven multi-agent collaboration system, coupled with a contract knowledge base, then automatically generates a compact customized inference framework that satisfies these constraints. We evaluate metainfer from three perspectives: the effect of source-code reference, the runtime behavior and performance profile of engines generated under the zero-reference constraint on CKB-covered targets, and knowledge-base evolution for new model and platform scenarios. The results show that metainfer organizes generation constraints, validation feedback, and knowledge consolidation into a continuous closed loop, enabling runnable customized inference solutions to be generated from explicit knowledge. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MetaInfer/MetaInfer.

AI.tldr: metainfer is an "LLM-as-Compiler" framework that automatically generates customized inference frameworks from user-specified runtime constraints using an LLM-driven multi-agent system and contract knowledge base.
AI.motivation: LLM technology advances rapidly, creating a complex landscape of model families, hardware, quantization schemes, parallelization strategies, and optimization kernels. This increases code complexity and maintenance costs in general-purpose inference frameworks. Conventional software engineering abstractions help but also add complexity and performance overhead.
AI.method: Users specify only runtime constraints. An LLM-driven multi-agent collaboration system, coupled with a contract knowledge base, automatically generates a compact customized inference framework that satisfies these constraints.
AI.result: Evaluated from three perspectives: effect of source-code reference, runtime behavior/performance on CKB-covered targets under zero-reference constraint, and knowledge-base evolution. Results show metainfer organizes generation constraints, validation feedback, and knowledge consolidation into a continuous closed loop, enabling runnable customized inference solutions from explicit knowledge.
AI.conclusion: metainfer effectively demonstrates that combining LLM-driven multi-agent collaboration with contract knowledge management can generate runnable customized inference solutions from explicit constraints, reducing code complexity and maintenance costs.

title: EFLUX: Elastic Multi-Robot Formation Navigation and Adaptation with Agentic LLMs
summary: Multi-robot teams operating in confined or cluttered environments must adapt both their formation geometry and group topology to navigate through complex obstacles. This adaptation requires two complementary behaviors: deformation, where the team continuously reshapes its geometry while remaining connected, and reconfiguration, where robots split into subgroups or merge back into a single formation. Existing methods often model these behaviors independently, connect them through handcrafted rules, or lack explicit geometric criteria for determining when each behavior should be invoked. However, challenging environments may require online changes in formation shape, connectivity, and effective team composition, making decoupled or rule-based approaches prone to suboptimal trajectories and deadlock. We propose EFLUX, a geometry-grounded LLM agentic framework for automatic and elastic multi-robot formation navigation. EFLUX extracts a structured scene representation and uses an LLM to reason jointly over both deformation actions, such as scaling and shearing, and reconfiguration actions, such as splitting and merging. These strategies are then translated into executable per-robot waypoints through a closed-loop generation, verification, and correction pipeline. Simulation and hardware experiments show that EFLUX enables safe, continuous, and elastic formation navigation in constrained environments, reducing deadlock and navigation failures compared with baselines while maintaining coherent multi-robot coordination.

AI.tldr: EFLUX is a geometry-grounded LLM framework for automatic and elastic multi-robot formation navigation that jointly handles deformation (scaling, shearing) and reconfiguration (splitting, merging) actions through a closed-loop generation, verification, and correction pipeline.
AI.motivation: Multi-robot teams in confined/cluttered environments must adapt both formation geometry and group topology. Existing methods model deformation and reconfiguration independently or use handcrafted rules, lacking explicit geometric criteria for when to invoke each behavior. This decoupled approach is prone to suboptimal trajectories and deadlock in challenging environments.
AI.method: EFLUX extracts a structured scene representation and uses an LLM to reason jointly over deformation actions (scaling, shearing) and reconfiguration actions (splitting, merging). These strategies are translated into executable per-robot waypoints through a closed-loop generation, verification, and correction pipeline.
AI.result: Simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate that EFLUX enables safe, continuous, and elastic formation navigation in constrained environments, reducing deadlock and navigation failures compared to baselines while maintaining coherent multi-robot coordination.
AI.conclusion: EFLUX addresses the limitations of decoupled or rule-based approaches by providing a unified, geometry-grounded LLM framework that can handle both deformation and reconfiguration online, making it more robust for complex navigation scenarios.

title: Enabling 24-hour Agricultural Robotics: Unsupervised Day-to-Night Cross-Modal Image Translation for Nighttime Visual Navigation
summary: While visual navigation has been extensively studied in agricultural robotics, most existing systems assume daytime conditions. In fact, deploying autonomous robots at night offers significant advantages, including 24-hour crop and soil monitoring, fruit harvesting, and nocturnal pest detection. Modern vision-based systems, however, rely heavily on large-scale well-annotated image datasets, which remains challenging to obtain for nighttime operation scenarios. To address this, we propose an unsupervised image translation framework that converts daytime plant-row RGB images into near-infrared (NIR) nighttime counterparts without requiring pixel-to-pixel supervision. This enables the direct reuse of daytime semantic labels for training nighttime perception models. In particular, by incorporating a pre-trained Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) model, the proposed framework is designed to preserve semantic consistency during day-to-night translation. Additionally, a visibility mask is introduced to account for the limited effective range of NIR illumination in nighttime scenes. We conduct comparative evaluations with state-of-the-art image translation baselines and demonstrate higher image qualities, as supported by improved performance in downstream semantic segmentation for nighttime visual navigation. For evaluation, we utilize AgriNight--a novel dataset comprising 428 daytime and 549 nighttime images collected using night-vision-equipped mobile robots in agricultural fields and manually annotated with pixel-wise semantic labels--and introduce it as the first benchmark for nighttime agricultural visual navigation. We also perform real-time autonomous navigation experiments with a physical robot operating at night. The data and code are available at: https://github.com/mamorobel/AgriNight.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an unsupervised image translation framework that converts daytime plant-row RGB images to near-infrared nighttime images without pixel-level supervision, using CLIP for semantic consistency and a visibility mask for limited NIR illumination. The approach is evaluated on a new AgriNight dataset, demonstrating higher image quality and improved semantic segmentation performance for nighttime agricultural navigation.
AI.motivation: Most agricultural visual navigation systems assume daytime conditions, but nighttime operation offers advantages like 24-hour monitoring, fruit harvesting, and pest detection. However, modern vision systems require large-scale well-annotated datasets, which are challenging to obtain for nighttime scenarios.
AI.method: The proposed framework performs unsupervised day-to-night image translation of plant-row RGB images to near-infrared nighttime counterparts without pixel-to-pixel supervision. It incorporates a pre-trained CLIP model to preserve semantic consistency and introduces a visibility mask to account for limited NIR illumination range. The approach leverages the AgriNight dataset for training and evaluation.
AI.result: The framework achieves higher image quality compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with improved performance in downstream semantic segmentation for nighttime navigation. Real-time autonomous navigation experiments with a physical robot operating at night demonstrate practical applicability.
AI.conclusion: The unsupervised translation framework enables direct reuse of daytime semantic labels for training nighttime perception models, overcoming the challenge of obtaining labeled nighttime data. The AgriNight dataset serves as the first benchmark for nighttime agricultural visual navigation, providing a foundation for future research in nocturnal agricultural robotics.

title: Robust In-Hand Manipulation via Priors in Reinforcement Learning and Mechanical Design
summary: In-hand manipulation without external sensing is challenging due to uncertainties from finger-object contacts and disturbances by gravity. While reinforcement learning has shown promise in learning complex finger gaiting, existing approaches do not prioritize maintaining well-conditioned grasps for sustained manipulation. We introduce two complementary physics priors for robust in-hand rolling: a global grasp-quality prior derived from classical grasp analysis and a local contact-geometry prior based on fingertip curvature. The grasp-quality prior is used as a dense reward-shaping term that encourages well-distributed contacts with improved worst-case wrench resistance. The contact-geometry prior is expressed in the fingertip geometry that mechanically shapes the contact interface toward task-aligned rolling while reducing off-axis drift. We evaluate the effect of these priors on learning in-hand rolling manipulation for a multifingered robotic hand manipulating three different objects at four palm orientations. Results show significant improvement in rotation efficiency, grasp stability, and disturbance rejection, suggesting that physics priors embedded in both learning and fingertip morphology improve task robustness and sim-to-real transfer. An overview video can be found at https://youtu.be/pdd1wHxQnJM?si=dM-U5kiiPTYsk3Pk.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces two physics priors (global grasp-quality and local contact-geometry) for in-hand rolling manipulation, demonstrating significant improvements in rotation efficiency, grasp stability, and disturbance rejection through both reward shaping and fingertip morphology design.
AI.motivation: In-hand manipulation without external sensing faces challenges from uncertainties in finger-object contacts and gravity disturbances. While reinforcement learning has shown promise for complex finger gaiting, existing approaches fail to prioritize maintaining well-conditioned grasps for sustained manipulation.
AI.method: The authors introduce two complementary physics priors: 1) A global grasp-quality prior derived from classical grasp analysis, used as a dense reward-shaping term to encourage well-distributed contacts with improved worst-case wrench resistance; 2) A local contact-geometry prior based on fingertip curvature, expressed in fingertip geometry to mechanically shape the contact interface toward task-aligned rolling while reducing off-axis drift. The approach is evaluated on a multifingered robotic hand manipulating three different objects at four palm orientations.
AI.result: Results show significant improvements in rotation efficiency, grasp stability, and disturbance rejection. The physics priors embedded in both learning and fingertip morphology demonstrate improved task robustness and enhanced sim-to-real transfer capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Physics priors, when integrated into both the learning framework (through reward shaping) and the physical design (through fingertip morphology), substantially improve in-hand manipulation performance. This approach enables more robust manipulation under uncertainties and facilitates successful transfer from simulation to real-world applications.

title: GaitSpan: Growing Humanoid Locomotion from Walking to Running
summary: A humanoid that can walk should not relearn locomotion from scratch to jog or run. Yet current approaches often obtain gait diversity by prescribing gait schedules, imitating motion clips, training experts to switch between or distilling skills into one policy. These strategies can produce impressive behaviors, but offer limited flexibility across continuous speed commands, terrains, and morphologies. We study skill growth with GaitSpan, a framework that expands a pretrained, basic walking policy into faster locomotion. It treats walking as a seed skill: reusable motor structure for balance, support, body coordination, and contact transition that can be regenerated at new rhythms, extended into longer/higher strides, and corrected by residual adaptation. This expansion has three aspects: 1) rhythm generation, which modulates the frozen walking policy with multiple internal clocks and learns command-conditioned combinations of the resulting canonical actions; 2) stride shaping, which rewards dynamic locomotion patterns appropriate for higher commanded speeds using a physically grounded objective inspired by spring-loaded inverted pendulum dynamics; and 3) residual adaptation, which captures motion details not accounted for by rhythm generation or stride shaping. GaitSpan is the first to deliver a single command-conditioned humanoid policy that spans walking, jogging, and running-like regimes covering a continuous speed range, transfers across morphologies, and deploys zero-shot on unseen sim-to-sim, and real-world terrains. Compared with baselines either trained with multi-experts or imitation from humans, it learns faster and achieves stronger gait performance.

AI.tldr: GaitSpan expands a pretrained walking policy into faster locomotion (jogging and running) by treating walking as a seed skill with rhythm generation, stride shaping, and residual adaptation, enabling a single policy to span walking, jogging, and running across continuous speeds.
AI.motivation: Current approaches to gait diversity (gait schedules, motion imitation, multi-expert training, skill distillation) have limited flexibility across continuous speed commands, terrains, and morphologies; the authors seek a unified policy that can continuously transition between walking, jogging, and running.
AI.method: GaitSpan treats walking as a reusable motor structure (seed skill) expanded in three ways: (1) rhythm generation modulates the frozen walking policy with internal clocks to create command-conditioned canonical actions; (2) stride shaping uses a physically grounded spring-loaded inverted pendulum objective to reward dynamic patterns for higher speeds; (3) residual adaptation captures details not covered by the first two components.
AI.result: GaitSpan delivers a single command-conditioned humanoid policy spanning walking, jogging, and running-like regimes across continuous speeds, transfers across morphologies, and deploys zero-shot on unseen sim-to-sim and real-world terrains, learning faster and achieving stronger gait performance than baselines.
AI.conclusion: GaitSpan successfully achieves continuous gait transition between walking, jogging, and running with transferability across morphologies and zero-shot deployment, demonstrating that treating walking as a seed skill with modular expansion can overcome the limitations of existing gait diversity approaches.

title: A Behavioral State Vocabulary in Sony ERS-111 R-CODE
summary: This paper presents a corpus-level analysis of generated behavior diagrams derived from Sony's R-CODE sample distribution for the ERS-111 AIBO. Rather than reading each script in isolation, the study compares named states across the corpus to identify the recurring control vocabulary that structures the sample set. The resulting aggregate shows that many superficially different routines are built from a compact embodied grammar centered on initialization, sensing, iterative action, synchronization, and recovery. In addition to historical analysis, the paper argues that this form of state-based abstraction is useful as an intermediate representation for constructing new encapsulated behavior routines, especially on constrained native robotic systems where deterministic control, direct hardware access, and modular behavioral composition remain important.

title: More than a Manipulator: Planning Propellant-Free Attitude Maneuvers for Free-Floating Spacecraft
summary: Spacecraft attitude control is traditionally achieved using momentum exchange devices or propellant-consuming thrusters. Meanwhile, a growing number of missions require robotic manipulators, which are typically treated as disturbance sources to be rejected rather than as actuators for spacecraft reorientation. This work investigates the use of manipulator motions for propellant-free attitude control by formulating a trajectory optimization problem with critical joint and collision avoidance constraints. Using an interior point solver for the resulting nonlinear program, complex slew and detumble trajectories are demonstrated for a range of spacecraft-manipulator systems with varying kinematic complexity and mass properties. The achievable control authority is compared directly with that of reaction wheel arrays via momentum and torque envelopes, demonstrating the potential for manipulators to serve as redundant or even primary attitude control systems. This work provides a framework for using manipulators as multipurpose attitude control actuators, with particularly promising applications in in-space assembly and manufacturing when grasping payloads with high relative mass fractions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates using robotic manipulators as propellant-free attitude control actuators for spacecraft, demonstrating that optimized manipulator motions can achieve attitude control comparable to reaction wheel arrays through trajectory optimization with collision avoidance constraints.
AI.motivation: Traditional spacecraft attitude control relies on momentum exchange devices (reaction wheels) or propellant-consuming thrusters. With growing mission requirements for robotic manipulators, these manipulators are typically treated as disturbance sources rather than as actuators for spacecraft reorientation. There is a need for propellant-free attitude control methods, especially for in-space assembly and manufacturing missions.
AI.method: The researchers formulated a trajectory optimization problem for spacecraft-manipulator attitude control that includes critical joint and collision avoidance constraints. They used an interior point solver to solve the resulting nonlinear program. The approach was tested on spacecraft-manipulator systems with varying kinematic complexity and mass properties to demonstrate complex slew and detumble trajectories.
AI.result: Complex slew and detumble trajectories were successfully demonstrated across various spacecraft-manipulator systems. The achievable control authority was directly compared with reaction wheel arrays using momentum and torque envelopes. The results show that manipulators can serve as redundant or even primary attitude control systems, with particular effectiveness when grasping payloads with high relative mass fractions.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a framework for using manipulators as multipurpose attitude control actuators, demonstrating that optimized manipulator motions can achieve propellant-free attitude control with control authority comparable to reaction wheel arrays. The approach is particularly promising for in-space assembly and manufacturing applications involving high-mass-fraction payloads.

title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game
comment: This paper has been accepted as a Late-Breaking Report to the 35th IEEE International Conference on Robot and Human Interactive Communication (RO-MAN), which will be held in Kitakyushu, Netherlands on August 24-28, 2026. summary: Robot gaze is a major component of human-robot dialogue coordination. Most studies of gaze in human-robot dialogue focus on face-to-face social conversations, but little is known about gaze in demanding task-focused interactions. In this paper, we investigate how the gaze of a robot game partner affects human visual attention and if humans tend to direct confirmation-seeking gazes towards the robot. In our study, we let participants play a collaborative word association game with a NAO robot acting as an embodied, LLM-driven conversational partner. Our experiments are conducted under two conditions, which implement mutual and referential gazes of the robot respectively. We record participants' gaze using eye tracking glasses and analyze the interactions using gaze coordinates, speech segments, key events and areas of interests. We find that robot gaze orientation does not affect the time to first fixation on words the robot proposed. We also find that participants gaze more often at the robot when their dialogue line contains confirmation requests, compared to when it does not. Our results indicate (likely also due to the cognitively demanding nature of the game) that the verbal aspect of this task overshadows the effects of referential robot gaze. These findings offer valuable insights for designing and validating robot gaze and turn-taking behavior in collaborative tasks which require coordination and efficient communication.

AI.tldr: This study investigates how a robot's gaze in a collaborative word association game affects human visual attention and whether humans direct confirmation-seeking gazes toward the robot.
AI.motivation: Most existing research on human-robot gaze focuses on face-to-face social conversations, with little understanding of gaze dynamics in demanding task-focused interactions.
AI.method: Participants played a collaborative word association game with an embodied NAO robot (LLM-driven). Two gaze conditions were implemented: mutual gaze and referential gaze. Gaze data was collected via eye tracking glasses and analyzed using gaze coordinates, speech segments, key events, and areas of interest.
AI.result: Robot gaze orientation did not affect the time to first fixation on words proposed by the robot. Participants gazed at the robot more frequently when their dialogue contained confirmation requests compared to when it did not.
AI.conclusion: The verbal aspect of the task overshadows the effects of referential robot gaze, likely due to the cognitively demanding nature of the game. These findings provide valuable insights for designing robot gaze and turn-taking behavior in collaborative tasks requiring coordination and efficient communication.

title: Contract-Grounded Behavior Tree Synthesis via Coding Agents
summary: Synthesizing deployable robot behavior trees (BTs) from natural language (NL) requires grounding to ensure every generated BT references only skills a robot can actually execute. Existing LLM-based BT synthesis approaches often place this grounding responsibility on the prompt author. This makes deployment brittle when the author does not know which skills the robot can execute, how those skills are parameterized, or how the robot runtime software constrains valid BT structure. This paper proposes a contract-grounded BT synthesis architecture in which a coding agent queries a robot-side Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to retrieve an explicit contract consisting of a skill library, permitted BT operators, and optional BT composition templates, before synthesizing a BT for validation and execution. In our framework, non-expert operators issue NL commands without knowledge of robot implementation details, while a robot runtime validation gate enforces correctness before execution. We evaluate two LLMs, a closed model (Sonnet 4.6) and a smaller open-source model (Gemma4:31b), across 110 simulated tasks in PyRoboSim and 14 tasks on a physical Husarion Panther robot. Results show that contract grounding enables near-perfect BT validation and high task success, that BT composition templates substantially recover success on reactive control-flow tasks for the smaller model, and that the architecture transfers to physical hardware running a Nav2 stack opaque to both operator and agent.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a contract-grounded BT synthesis architecture where a coding agent queries a robot-side MCP server to retrieve skill libraries and BT constraints before synthesizing behavior trees from natural language, enabling non-expert operators to issue commands while runtime validation ensures correctness.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM-based BT synthesis approaches place grounding responsibility on prompt authors, making deployment brittle when authors lack knowledge of robot capabilities, skill parameterizations, or runtime software constraints.
AI.method: A coding agent queries a robot-side Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to retrieve an explicit contract consisting of a skill library, permitted BT operators, and optional BT composition templates before synthesizing BTs from NL commands. A runtime validation gate enforces correctness before execution.
AI.result: Contract grounding enables near-perfect BT validation and high task success across 124 total tasks (110 simulated in PyRoboSim, 14 physical on Husarion Panther). BT composition templates substantially recover success on reactive control-flow tasks for the smaller model. The architecture transfers to physical hardware running a Nav2 stack opaque to both operator and agent.
AI.conclusion: The contract-grounded approach enables robust BT synthesis without requiring prompt authors to have expert knowledge of robot implementation details, skill parameterizations, or runtime constraints.

title: DiffRadar: Differentiable Physics-Aware Radar SLAM with Gaussian Fields
summary: Radar sensing is increasingly used in mobile systems because it operates reliably under poor lighting, adverse weather, and privacy-sensitive settings where cameras and LiDAR often fail. However, most existing radar SLAM systems estimate motion through scan matching on discretized radar heatmaps, which breaks geometric continuity and fails to capture key radar sensing properties, often leading to unstable pose estimation and degraded mapping in regenerate or dynamically changing environments. We present DiffRadar, a real-time radar SLAM system that models radar observations as a differentiable, physics-aware Gaussian field rather than discrete scans. DiffRadar represents the scene as anisotropic Gaussian primitives and renders radar measurements in range-azimuth and Doppler-azimuth spaces through a differentiable radar forward model, enabling joint optimization of robot pose and scene structure directly from radar measurements. We implement DiffRadar on commodity FMCW radar hardware and evaluate it on both the public Radarize benchmark and a controlled stress-test suite that targets common radar SLAM failure modes, including corridor degeneracy, motion regime transitions, dynamic clutter, and long-horizon loop closures. DiffRadar achieves substantial reductions in trajectory error on the benchmark, with especially large gains under feature-poor corridor motion, while more than doubling map consistency and maintaining real-time performance at 70 FPS. These results show that modeling radar observations directly in the signal domain enables substantially more robust and consistent radar-only SLAM for mobile platforms.

AI.tldr: DiffRadar is a real-time radar SLAM system that models radar observations as differentiable, physics-aware Gaussian fields rather than discrete scans, achieving 70 FPS performance with substantially reduced trajectory errors and doubled map consistency.
AI.motivation: Existing radar SLAM systems estimate motion through scan matching on discretized radar heatmaps, which breaks geometric continuity and fails to capture key radar sensing properties, leading to unstable pose estimation and degraded mapping in challenging environments.
AI.method: DiffRadar represents the scene as anisotropic Gaussian primitives and renders radar measurements in range-azimuth and Doppler-azimuth spaces through a differentiable radar forward model, enabling joint optimization of robot pose and scene structure directly from radar measurements.
AI.result: DiffRadar achieves substantial reductions in trajectory error on the Radarize benchmark, especially large gains under feature-poor corridor motion, more than doubles map consistency, and maintains real-time performance at 70 FPS.
AI.conclusion: Modeling radar observations directly in the signal domain enables substantially more robust and consistent radar-only SLAM for mobile platforms.

title: Flatness-Preserving Residual Learning for Real-Time Tight Quadrotor Formation Flight
summary: Quadrotors flying in tight formations are severely affected by turbulent aerodynamic interactions, such as downwash, that can cause catastrophic collisions if left unmodeled. To compensate for these effects, we propose a physics-informed residual dynamics learning framework that captures complex aerodynamic interactions while ensuring the joint multi-quadrotor system remains differentially flat. We leverage this preserved flatness to design a computationally efficient feedback linearization controller that is easily tunable with linear control techniques and cancels aerodynamic disturbances via feedforward compensation. Hardware experiments demonstrate our framework reduces average tracking errors by 31% compared to nominal baselines. Crucially, our lightweight approach matches the tracking performance of state-of-the-art nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) while requiring an order of magnitude less computation. We are the first to show that stable, tight formation flight can be achieved with under 30 seconds of training data and a 5ms loop rate, unlocking high-fidelity aerodynamic compensation for compute-constrained flight stacks.

AI.tldr: A physics-informed residual dynamics learning framework that preserves differential flatness for quadrotor tight formations, enabling computationally efficient feedback linearization control with 31% tracking error reduction and matching state-of-the-art NMPC performance with an order of magnitude less computation.
AI.motivation: Quadrotors in tight formations suffer from turbulent aerodynamic interactions (e.g., downwash) that can cause catastrophic collisions if unmodeled, necessitating effective compensation strategies.
AI.method: A physics-informed residual dynamics learning framework that captures complex aerodynamic interactions while ensuring the joint multi-quadrotor system remains differentially flat. This preserved flatness enables a computationally efficient feedback linearization controller that is tunable via linear control techniques and cancels aerodynamic disturbances through feedforward compensation.
AI.result: Hardware experiments demonstrate 31% reduction in average tracking errors compared to nominal baselines. The approach matches state-of-the-art NMPC performance while requiring an order of magnitude less computation. Stable tight formation flight achieved with under 30 seconds of training data and 5ms loop rate.
AI.conclusion: First to demonstrate stable tight formation flight with under 30 seconds of training data and 5ms loop rate, unlocking high-fidelity aerodynamic compensation for compute-constrained flight stacks.

title: Reducing Temporal Redundancy for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit strong generalization for robotic manipulation, yet their high inference latency limits real time deployment. We identify two primary sources of temporal redundancy in existing VLA pipelines: repeated visual encoding of highly similar consecutive frames and multi step iterative sampling in diffusion based policies. To address this, we propose a system level acceleration strategy that reduces computation in both perception and action generation. On the perception side, we incrementally update only tokens corresponding to dynamic scene regions instead of re-encoding entire frames. On the policy side, we compress diffusion sampling into a compact 2-step schedule through efficiency oriented training while preserving action precision. Experiments on Libero, RobotWin, and Real Robot Platforms demonstrate over 2 times speedup while maintaining high performance, achieving up to 98% success rate on general manipulation benchmarks. Our codes will be released on Github.

AI.tldr: A system-level acceleration strategy that reduces temporal redundancy in VLA models by incrementally updating dynamic scene tokens in perception and compressing diffusion sampling into 2 steps in policy generation, achieving over 2x speedup with 98% success rate.
AI.motivation: VLA models generalize well for robotic manipulation but suffer from high inference latency that limits real-time deployment. Two primary sources of temporal redundancy are identified: (1) repeated visual encoding of highly similar consecutive frames, and (2) multi-step iterative sampling in diffusion-based policies.
AI.method: Two-pronged approach: (1) Perception: Incrementally update only tokens corresponding to dynamic scene regions instead of re-encoding entire frames; (2) Policy: Compress diffusion sampling into a compact 2-step schedule through efficiency-oriented training while preserving action precision.
AI.result: Experiments on Libero, RobotWin, and Real Robot Platforms demonstrate over 2 times speedup while maintaining high performance, achieving up to 98% success rate on general manipulation benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The proposed system-level acceleration strategy effectively reduces computation in both perception and action generation components without sacrificing performance, making VLA models more suitable for real-time robotic deployment.

title: VistaVLA: Geometry- and Semantic-Aware 3D Gaussian-Grounded VLA for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful end-to-end paradigm for robotic manipulation by mapping language instructions and 2D visual inputs directly to actions. However, these models lack an explicit, scene-level 3D representation, limiting their ability to reason over spatial layouts and geometric constraints. While recent efforts incorporate explicit 3D cues, such as depth maps or point clouds, to improve geometric awareness, they primarily capture low-level structures and lack high-level semantic grounding in 3D space. In human cognition, interaction with the physical world relies on a 3D semantic cognitive map - an internal mental model that integrates spatial layouts with semantic context to enable persistent, viewpoint-invariant reasoning. In light of this, we present VistaVLA, a novel two-stage framework that constructs a geometry- and semantics-aware 3D cognitive representation from 3D Gaussian primitives and grounds it as compact context tokens for VLA policy learning. Specifically, VistaVLA lifts multi-view vision-language features into 3D Gaussian primitives, forming geometry-anchored semantic tokens that align view-consistent spatial grounding with 2D visual feature spaces. To make this 3D representation computationally tractable for effective VLA control, we introduce Merge-then-Query (MtQ), a token summarization mechanism. MtQ compresses dense Gaussian primitives into a highly compact set of spatially informative tokens, achieving a 99% token reduction while preserving action-relevant 3D layouts and semantic context. Extensive evaluations in both simulated and real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness of VistaVLA. Notably, in real-world scenarios, VistaVLA improves success rates by 22.8% across seven real-world tasks and by 30.0% over the VLA-Adapter baseline on challenging out-of-distribution tasks.

AI.tldr: VistaVLA is a two-stage framework that constructs a geometry- and semantics-aware 3D cognitive representation from 3D Gaussian primitives, using Merge-then-Query token summarization to enable effective VLA policy learning for robotic manipulation.
AI.motivation: VLA models lack explicit scene-level 3D representation, limiting spatial reasoning capabilities. Recent approaches with depth maps or point clouds capture low-level structures but lack high-level semantic grounding in 3D space, unlike human cognitive maps that integrate spatial layouts with semantic context for viewpoint-invariant reasoning.
AI.method: VistaVLA lifts multi-view vision-language features into 3D Gaussian primitives to form geometry-anchored semantic tokens. It introduces Merge-then-Query (MtQ), a token summarization mechanism that compresses dense Gaussian primitives into a highly compact set of spatially informative tokens, achieving 99% token reduction while preserving action-relevant 3D layouts and semantic context.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations in simulated and real-world environments demonstrate VistaVLA's effectiveness. In real-world scenarios, VistaVLA improves success rates by 22.8% across seven real-world tasks and by 30.0% over the VLA-Adapter baseline on challenging out-of-distribution tasks.
AI.conclusion: VistaVLA successfully bridges the gap between 3D cognitive representation and VLA policy learning by providing geometry- and semantics-aware spatial grounding that enables more robust robotic manipulation in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios.

title: StratMamba: Strategic and Reactive Stream Partitioning for Path-Efficient LiDAR-Based Obstacle Avoidance
comment: Accepted to IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026). 8 pages, 6 figures. Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z0FfO_AVaSw
summary: This paper proposes StratMamba, a dual-stream Mamba-based temporal modeling architecture, to more efficiently capture long-horizon temporal dependencies required for robot navigation in complex and obstacle-rich environments. StratMamba leverages a combination of fast-decay and slow-decay memory architectures, where the fast-decay component processes high-frequency LiDAR data for reactive obstacle avoidance, while the slow-decay component maintains longer-horizon goal information for strategic planning. We perform extensive evaluations of different obstacle avoidance scenarios in IsaacLab and Gazebo, while also validating successful sim-to-real deployment on a Unitree GO1 quadruped robot navigating in the presence of static/dynamic obstacles. Comparisons with other temporal RL baselines, such as LSTM, Transformer, and Vanilla-Mamba, show that our StratMamba achieves exceptional temporal reasoning efficiency with a lower timeout rate, while maintaining the fastest navigation speed (576 median steps, 5.0% better than Vanilla-Mamba). It also achieves the highest path optimality (0.915 path efficiency) across all baselines. Real-world evaluation reveals that StratMamba maintains more robust performance across extended LiDAR ranges compared to vanilla Mamba and the Transformer, demonstrating that dual-stream partitioning effectively balances reactive safety with strategic navigation under challenging sensing conditions.
